title: Improve per-collector error handling + partial bundle rendering (fail-open, clear retry hints)
author: Jacob Stein
description:
Context: responders have flagged that when a context bundle is missing sections, it is unclear whether (a) the bot didn’t run that collector, (b) the collector timed out, (c) upstream data is delayed, or (d) redaction removed most content. This PR makes the bundle explicitly fail-open with per-collector status blocks, clearer error text, and actionable retry hints so responders can trust what’s missing and why. It also improves internal error typing so we can track collector health without spamming #incidents.

What’s in this PR: (1) CollectorResult now carries a first-class status: ok | partial | timeout | upstream_unavailable | redacted | error, plus duration_ms and optional retry_after_seconds. (2) Bundle rendering always includes a short “Collector status” section (collapsed by default in Slack) listing each collector with an icon + status + duration + short reason. (3) Each collector section now renders either data OR a bounded error block with: what failed, what we tried, and a single next action (“Retry in ~2m”, “Use dashboard link”, or “Run /incident-bot diagnostics <collector>”). (4) Explicitly distinguishes timeouts vs upstream failures vs internal errors. Timeouts show “collector exceeded 1.5s budget” and include retry hint; upstream failures include endpoint name and a correlation id; internal errors include sanitized exception class only (no payload). (5) Adds a “partial bundle” banner at top when any required collector is not ok. Banner includes a single safe-to-post line and a link to internal docs for deeper diagnostics.

Behavioral changes: - The bot will still post a bundle even if 1+ collectors fail. - Missing sections are never silently omitted. - Retries are NOT automatic in this PR; we only surface hints and a manual command for deeper diagnostics. - Restricted-mode redaction remains unchanged; however, redacted collectors now show status=redacted rather than appearing broken.

Slack formatting: - Status line uses a stable order: deploys -> config diff -> saturation -> links. - Collector blocks are truncated to 4 lines max with “Show more” expansion where supported. - Timestamps are always rendered as absolute UTC + “(x min ago)”.

Telemetry: - Adds counter incidentbot.collector.result{collector,status} and histogram incidentbot.collector.duration_ms{collector}. - Adds incidentbot.bundle.partial counter when any required collector is not ok. These are intended for internal dashboards / alerting (follow-up in ENG-2845).

Testing: - Unit tests for error mapping (timeout vs upstream vs internal). - Snapshot tests for Slack block rendering across ok/partial/timeout/upstream/redacted cases. - Adds a regression test for INT-1188 (too-verbose error dumps) ensuring we never render stack traces or payload excerpts.

Rollout note: no config changes required. This is safe behind existing feature flag (incident_bot.collectors.enabled). Once merged, responders should see status blocks on the next incident bundle.

Screenshots / examples (sanitized): Example when saturation metrics lag: “Saturation (timeout): metrics query exceeded 1500ms budget. Retry in ~120s or open dashboard: <link> (corr=mbx-7f1c)”. Example when config snapshot endpoint 503s: “Config diff (upstream unavailable): config-snapshot service returned 503 (region=us-east). Retry in ~60s or check change feed dashboard.”

Related: ENG-2845 (hardening/timeouts/circuit breakers), INT-1188 (verbosity), and feedback in #incidents about missing-data trust.
commits: render: add per-collector status section + partial bundle banner
errors: map timeouts/upstream/internal to sanitized user-facing messages
telemetry: export collector result counters + duration histogram
tests: snapshot slack blocks for error/timeout/redacted cases
review_conversation:
Rafael Mendes (review): This is the right direction. Two asks: (1) Make sure the status section is compact enough to not push real data below the fold in Slack, and (2) please ensure we never render raw exception messages from upstream (some include URLs with query params).

Jacob Stein (author): Ack. I’ll cap status lines and switch upstream error rendering to a sanitized shape (service + http status + corr id only). Will push an update.

Sean Gallagher (review): Love the “partial bundle” banner. Can we standardize the next action text so responders aren’t guessing? E.g. always either “Retry in N seconds” or “Open dashboard” or “Run /incident-bot diagnostics …”. Also: do we still post the bundle if deploy collector fails? (we should).

Jacob Stein (author): Yep, bundle always posts. I’ll normalize the action language and make deploy failure show as status=error with retry hint.

Allison Grant (review): Telemetry labels look good but please keep status cardinality bounded. Don’t include dynamic upstream names or exception classes in metric labels. Also request: duration histogram should be per-collector only.

Jacob Stein (author): Done. status is one of the fixed enum values; collector is a fixed name set. Upstream service name stays in logs only.

Marcus Lin (security review): Confirm we’re not leaking payload/token content in Slack. I see we’re now including correlation ids — are those safe to post in #incidents? We typically allow request/trace ids but not customer ids.

Jacob Stein (author): Corr id is an internal incident-bot request id (random UUID, no customer linkage). Added comment + test to ensure we never propagate upstream request ids or query strings.

Rafael Mendes (follow-up): One more nit: the banner says “collector timeout exceeded 1500ms budget” — can we avoid implying an SLO guarantee? Maybe “collector exceeded its time budget” is fine.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated wording in render templates.

Approvals: Rafael Mendes approved; Sean Gallagher approved; Allison Grant approved; Marcus Lin approved.

Merge: Squash merged into main.
release_notes: Incident bot now renders explicit per-collector status for partial context bundles (timeouts/upstream failures/redaction), with compact retry hints and sanitized error messaging. Bundles always fail-open and no longer silently omit missing sections.
